entries.title: Provider abstraction: six adapters, never assume Claude
entries.summary: src/providers/index.ts registers exactly six LlmProvider adapters -- claude, codex, copilot, agy, opencode, none -- matching the LlmProvider union at src/types.ts:4. There is no gemini adapter. Any auth, credential or dispatch change must route through the ProviderAdapter interface rather than assuming Claude-specific fields, and getProvider() defaults to claude only when the argument is null/undefined.

entries.title: Same-slug callers now open two SqliteProvider handles on one kb.sqlite
entries.summary: Keying the KB provider cache by (slug, repoPath) means two local clones of the same remote get two separate SqliteProvider instances pointed at the same kb.sqlite file; this is safe by design because init sets WAL plus busy_timeout=5000.

entries.title: A missing-anchor freshness regression surfaces first as kb_list dropping entries, not as a stale-flag assertion
entries.summary: In tests/knowledge/kb-remote-member-e2e.test.ts the four remote-member assertions live in one it(), so removing SqliteProvider's anchorIsMissing guard fails at the SAME DATABASE read-back (line 165) and never reaches the raw stale-row check (line 181).

entries.title: KB provider cache is now keyed by (slug, repoPath), not slug alone
entries.summary: getKbProviders/_providers Map keys on providerKey(slug, repoPath) via a NUL join, so two callers resolving to the same project slug but different repoPath values get distinct provider instances, each anchored at its own caller's repoPath.

entries.title: secure.NAME token values arrive already shell-escaped, and the escaping is OS-branched
entries.summary: execute_command replaces each secure.NAME token with a value that has ALREADY been quoted for the target member's shell -- escapePowerShellArg for windows members, escapeShellArg otherwise, chosen from agentOs. Reference the token bare in a command string; wrapping it in your own quotes double-escapes the value and surfaces as a false 401 or invalid-token error. This entry deliberately writes the token without its surrounding double braces: kb_session_prime injects KB entries verbatim into every agent dispatch prompt, and execute_prompt rejects any prompt matching the braced secure-token pattern, so spelling it in full here makes every dispatch in a sprint fail.

entries.title: bd prints literal JSON null, not [], for an empty dolt remote list
entries.summary: `bd dolt remote list --json` emits the JSON literal null when no Dolt remotes are configured. parseDoltRemoteList maps that to [] before its non-array guard, so an unwired repo reads as "no remotes" rather than a parse error; every other non-array shape still throws. Without the null branch, checkDoltRemoteAbsent returns ok:false ("could not parse") for a repo that is simply not wired to a Dolt remote.

entries.title: Local members use host OAuth; provision_llm_auth skips them
entries.summary: Local fleet members share the orchestrator's own machine, so they use whatever OAuth session is already active on that host. provision_llm_auth explicitly skips local members rather than attempting to provision credentials for them.

entries.title: A throw from a mocked execute_command is degraded, not propagated, under failSoft
entries.summary: WorkflowEngine._commandDispatch converts a transport-level rejection into { ok: false, error: <message> } when opts.failSoft is set, so a fail-closed throw inside the mock-sprint harness surfaces as a soft failure message rather than unwinding the sprint.

entries.title: sprint-logs/ must never carry a blanket directory ignore -- .gitignore says so inline
entries.summary: A directory-level rule such as '/sprint-logs/' shadows everything beneath it, un-ignore patterns included, and silently breaks the sprint cost ledger because auto-sprint.js stages it with an unguarded `git add sprint-logs/`. Merged main keeps only scoped rules and records the prohibition as a comment in .gitignore itself, so the lesson survives without depending on the KB.

entries.title: kb-setup is the one kb tool that takes repo_path but resolves no KB
entries.summary: Fifteen of the sixteen src/tools/kb-*.ts tools spread kbScopeFields and forward repo_remote_url to getKbProviders; kb-setup is excluded by design because its repo_path only locates a .git dir for hook installation and it writes a single global config, never selecting a project KB.

entries.title: The supervisor's dolt-orphan-sweep arms on a 5-minute interval with no immediate first pass
entries.summary: createDoltOrphanSweep().start() only arms a setInterval(DEFAULT_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS = 5 min) and never runs sweepOnce() eagerly, so a supervisor process that lives under 5 minutes never sweeps at all -- the basis for any time-bounded mitigation of its machine-wide kill scope.

entries.title: sandbox-lock.mjs has no read-only ownership query, so ordering around release is load-bearing
entries.summary: authorizeAndReleaseLock both authorizes and unlinks in one call, and the CLI exposes only acquire/mark-server-started/release -- so any Teardown step placed BEFORE the release runs unconditionally, including against a sandbox owned by a different live run.

entries.title: hasOppositePolarity matches on word-boundary regexes, not substrings
entries.summary: audn.ts hasOppositePolarity tests NEGATIVE_PATTERNS/POSITIVE_PATTERNS with precompiled word-boundary regexes, so "prefixed" no longer collides with "fixed".

entries.title: apra-fleet-se's plain npm test never sets APRA_FLEET_TEST_CONCURRENCY
entries.summary: packages/apra-fleet-se's "test" script runs node --test directly with --test-concurrency=8, but does NOT set the APRA_FLEET_TEST_CONCURRENCY env var -- only the separate test:unit/test:integration/test:record scripts (which route through scripts/run-tests.mjs) set it. A scaledTimeout()/waitFor() call that relies on the env var being set will silently use an unscaled timeout under plain npm test.

entries.title: raiseVcsPrForMember degrades every auth failure, including pre-PR provisioning, instead of throwing
entries.summary: As of the 5co8.15 fix, raiseVcsPrForMember catches a provisionPrCapableAuthForMember failure and returns authFailure:true rather than throwing, so both callers (Publish PR and finalizeAbort) skip the PR and let the sprint keep its computed verdict.

entries.title: One anchor policy, three branches: verbatim for read tools, hard-fail for kb_export
entries.summary: kb_session_prime and kb_stats pass a supplied repo_path to getKbProviders verbatim so an unreachable remote anchor stays honestly missing; kb_export deliberately keeps throwing instead, because it writes into repo_path -- and it throws before getKbProviders, so it never anchors at the server cwd either.

entries.title: The regression playbook 18300-series port claim came from a test-only base port, not a product constant
entries.summary: regression-test-playbook.md's old '18300-series fleet-sprint dashboard ports' rationale traces to packages/apra-fleet-se/test/spawner.test.mjs:629, which picks a random base port in 18300-18499 for test isolation. No product constant defines an 183xx range.

entries.title: Node's process.platform is win32 under Git Bash even though the invoking shell is POSIX-like
entries.summary: A Node script invoked from Git Bash on Windows sees process.platform === 'win32' (native node.exe), so platform-detection in a helper script should branch on process.platform, never on which shell/tools (lsof, pgrep) happen to be on PATH -- that lets a script correctly pick the Windows-native probe (netstat/taskkill, Get-CimInstance) even when run from a POSIX-shaped shell.

entries.title: kill-port.mjs owns the playbook's bounded-retry port-guard semantics, so playbook guards are one-liners
entries.summary: Every regression-playbook port guard (18700, 18701, 3001) is a single kill-port.mjs invocation; the 5s bounded retry, re-kill-each-pass, probe-tool hard-fail and fail-loud exit all live in waitPortFree(), not in the playbook's shell.

entries.title: The .trim() guard in resolveProjectSlug is provably redundant and cannot be pinned by any test
entries.summary: project-slug.ts guards its remote-URL short-circuit twice, but the outer remoteUrl.trim() check is unreachable-by-effect given slugify, so no input can distinguish its removal and no regression test can pin it.

entries.title: apra-fleet-5co8.40's closed status does not reflect its acceptance criteria being met
entries.summary: Bead apra-fleet-5co8.40 (curl/wget basename matching for absolute-path invocations) is marked closed, but CURL_WGET_TOKEN_RE in mock-sprint-harness.mjs is still an exact-match regex with zero test cases for path-prefixed curl/wget invocations -- the described fix was never implemented despite the close.

entries.title: kill-port netstat parsing depends on the colon-anchored port suffix
entries.summary: parseNetstatPids matches the local address with endsWith(':<port>'); the leading colon is what stops port 3001 from also matching netstat rows for 13001/23001/53001.

entries.title: The smoke test's supervisor uptime bound is enforced in Test scenario step 4, not in Teardown
entries.summary: Teardown's SUPERVISOR_UPTIME >= 300 check only prints a warning; the actual enforcement of the dolt-orphan-sweep mitigation is step 4's UPTIME_DEADLINE = SUPERVISOR_STARTED_AT + 280 hard-stop, so any regression test must assert on the 280s branch.

entries.title: Member OS resolution: always via agent.os
entries.summary: The orchestrator and each fleet member can independently run Windows/Mac/Linux -- local members share the orchestrator's own OS, but remote members can be any OS regardless of the orchestrator's. Never assume a target member's shell/OS matches the orchestrator's.

entries.title: Setup shell's $$ is unsafe to record for liveness checks under Git Bash on Windows
entries.summary: scripts/sandbox-lock.mjs's acquire CLI previously recorded the Setup shell's self-reported $$, which under Git Bash on Windows is an MSYS-internal pid invisible to defaultDeps.isAlive's native process.kill(pid,0) check -- fixed by having the CLI record its own process.ppid instead, since the CLI process is itself a direct child of the Setup shell and process.ppid always resolves in the native OS pid namespace.

entries.title: Verbatim-invocation criteria are unsatisfiable for the slow lane
entries.summary: An acceptance criterion demanding verbatim invocation of the regression slow-lane command conflicts with the same bead's ban on running the 8-minute lane, so the reachable evidence is the redirect shape plus a sandboxed stand-in.

entries.title: Local vs remote member dispatch paths
entries.summary: Local members share the orchestrator's own machine and credentials, so no SSH or file probe is needed -- check agent.agentType === 'local' and short-circuit. Remote members require actual SSH connectivity and credential probes.

entries.title: A directly launched sprint's deployer self-id is the branch name, not a ledger uuid
entries.summary: runner.js derives the deployer's own reservation id as validated.runId || validated.branch, so a standalone (non-supervisor) launch hands the deployer a branch name rather than a supervisor sprintId.

entries.title: gitRepos is an access list; only a single URL-shaped entry is a usable origin
entries.summary: agent.gitRepos is declared string[] and holds bare "Owner/Repo" access identifiers, not clone URLs. knownRepoRemoteUrl (now in src/services/member-remote-url.ts, re-exported from execute-prompt.ts) returns a URL only when gitRepos has EXACTLY one entry AND that entry is scheme-qualified; anything else yields undefined rather than a guessed URL.

entries.title: apra-fleet-client's createWorkflowEngine() is dead code -- workflow/ dir does not exist in that package
entries.summary: packages/apra-fleet-client/src/client/factory.mjs's createWorkflowEngine imports '../workflow/index.mjs' relative to itself, but apra-fleet-client's own src/ tree has no workflow/ directory in this repo state -- any caller must build the client manually (StdioTransport + McpClient + ApraFleet) instead.

entries.title: A sprint's own reservation is always in GET /api/sprints while it deploys
entries.summary: The supervisor reservation ledger always contains the deploying sprint's own entry, so any 'non-empty sprints array => stop' deploy gate blocks every sprint from deploying its own work; identity must be compared exactly on sprintId.

entries.title: The sprint run id reaches runner.js only via buildRunnerArgs' run_id key
entries.summary: spawner --run-id -> cli.mjs effectiveRunId existed but was dropped at buildRunnerArgs, so runner.js had no reservation identity; run_id must be added to both buildRunnerArgs and runner.js KNOWN_ARG_KEYS/validateArgs.

entries.title: Lockfile drift is invisible to npm test
entries.summary: A PR review that runs only 'npm test' cannot catch package.json/package-lock.json drift (e.g. a dependency override added to package.json without regenerating the lockfile), because npm test runs against whatever node_modules is already populated. Only 'npm ci' -- the reproducible-install path CI actually uses -- reproduces that failure.

entries.title: registerAllTools can be driven by a 4-line fake McpServer, unlocking every handler body for testing
entries.summary: The 'no test loads tool-registry.ts' gap is structural but trivially closable: a fake with tool()/server.sendLoggingMessage() records every registered handler and runs in ~2s.

entries.title: resolveProjectSlug prefers an explicit git remote URL over shelling git against repo_path
entries.summary: resolveProjectSlug(cwd, remoteUrl) slugifies remoteUrl directly when supplied and only falls back to `git remote get-url origin` against cwd, then the repo dirname, then 'default', when no URL is given -- letting remote members (whose repo_path is unreachable from the fleet server host) resolve to the same slug as a local clone.

entries.title: SqliteProvider freshness verdicts must be suppressed, not re-hashed, when the repo anchor is unreachable
entries.summary: A repo_path that does not exist on this host (the remote-member case) must never fall back to process.cwd() as the freshness anchor, and must not be re-hashed against it either -- both checkFreshness and freshnessSweep now short-circuit to a no-op verdict via a shared anchorIsMissing() check instead.

entries.title: A fallback message sharing the assertion's alternate keyword makes a test vacuous
entries.summary: checkDoltRemoteAbsent's bd-unavailable fallback messages all contain the word "unavailable", so the old combined assertion /Dolt-level remotes|unavailable/ was satisfied on any machine without bd without ever reaching the parser under test. Merged main closes this by probing bd --version first and asserting the two cases separately. The reusable trap: never OR an assertion's success keyword with its own fallback keyword.

entries.title: An unguarded cat of a shell marker file degrades to a wrong diagnosis, not a loud failure
entries.summary: regression-test-playbook.md's poll loop computed UPTIME_DEADLINE=$(( SUPERVISOR_STARTED_AT + 280 )) from an uncheck-ed cat; a missing marker made it evaluate to a bare 280, exiting 1 with the dolt-orphan-sweep tick message and sending operators after a nonexistent timing bug.

entries.title: In Git Bash, a background job's $! is an MSYS pid that never equals the process's own process.pid
entries.summary: Under MSYS/MinGW bash on Windows, $! returns the MSYS-internal pid while a spawned native Node process reports a different native Windows pid via process.pid, so any script that proves identity by comparing $! against a pid the process reports about itself can never match.

entries.title: normalizeMsysPathForPlatform is the required seam before path.resolve on any env-sourced path
entries.summary: Node's path.resolve does not understand MSYS /c/... paths and on win32 prefixes them with the current drive, so any filesystem path arriving from a Git Bash environment variable must go through normalizeMsysPathForPlatform first.

entries.title: StdioTransport.stop() is synchronous -- awaiting it with .catch() throws a TypeError
entries.summary: apra-fleet-client's StdioTransport.stop() returns undefined, so the common teardown idiom `await stop().catch(() => {})` throws TypeError inside a finally block and skips the cleanup after it.

entries.title: .fleet/ mixes a tracked deliverable (kb-canonical.json) with per-round scratch (planner-output.json)
entries.summary: Before adding a .gitignore rule under .fleet/, check git ls-files first -- .fleet/kb-canonical.json is a tracked, checked-in KB export deliverable, so a blanket '.fleet/' ignore rule would silently shadow it exactly the way this repo's own sprint-logs/ note warns against for directory-level ignore rules.

entries.title: Four resolveRepoPath helpers exist in src/tools, but only prime and stats ever had the null-to-cwd shape
entries.summary: kb-session-prime.ts and kb-stats.ts returned string|null and degraded to process.cwd(); kb-export.ts and kb-import.ts have always returned string and thrown, so they were never part of the b4g.7 anchor defect despite the bead naming kb-export as a third instance.

entries.title: regression-test-playbook.md's Setup/Reset/Teardown headings appear as backticked prose mentions elsewhere in the file, so naive string.split('## Setup') is unsafe
entries.summary: Any script or test that wants to isolate the Setup/Reset/Teardown sections of regression-test-playbook.md by splitting on the heading text must anchor to a whole line (e.g. /^## Setup$/m), not do a plain substring split -- the file's own intro and cross-reference prose repeatedly mentions `## Setup`, `## Reset`, `## Teardown` inside backticks well before the real headings, and a plain .split('## Setup')[1] picks up that prose fragment instead of the actual section body.

entries.title: mock-sprint network guard misses absolute-path curl invocations
entries.summary: isNetworkShapedCommand() matches only a bare curl/wget token, so an absolute-path invocation like /usr/bin/curl reaches the real runCmd() fallback and the host network.

entries.title: kb_session_prime must pass an explicit repo_path to getKbProviders verbatim, never through resolveRepoPath
entries.summary: Validating repo_path before handing it to getKbProviders converts a remote member's unreachable path into the fleet server's own cwd, silently staling healthy entries in the shared project KB; the anchor must stay honestly missing.

entries.title: dolt-orphan-sweep owner scoping is opt-in via FLEET_SE_SWEEP_OWNER_DATA_DIR, and must stay opt-in
entries.summary: buildSweepCommand() accepts an owner data-dir prefix that both shell families enforce, wired by bin/serve.mjs from FLEET_SE_SWEEP_OWNER_DATA_DIR; it cannot be derived from FLEET_SE_DATA_DIR because the ephemeral --data-dir belongs to the member, not the supervisor.
